findings.claim: The daemon owns native sessions and state; HTTP/SSE/web UI are projections and controls.
findings.implication: Keep LVX sessions alive independently of graph views.

findings.claim: Claude and Codex launch native interactive CLIs with session resume/fork identity and optional model/effort flags.
findings.implication: Preserve provider-native conversation IDs and model/effort choices without generic chat emulation.

findings.claim: Gemini is not built in; community harness readiness is weaker and fork is unsupported.
findings.implication: Build and independently capability-test a Gemini native adapter.

findings.claim: Native executable preservation does not imply prompt/config preservation: startup can project guidance/skills/hooks and launch settings.
findings.implication: Do not import OpenRig's full bootstrap as LVX default.

findings.claim: Claude selected agent prompts can replace the default main-agent prompt; appended prompt changes may remain pending.
findings.implication: No default role synthesis or invisible system-prompt replacement.

findings.claim: Peer messages use bracketed paste and explicit From/To envelopes; native terminal shells need a separate unwrapped path.
findings.implication: Use exact full message bodies and explicit source/target metadata, with transport-specific escaping.

findings.claim: Busy or unknown target readiness normally sends with advisory; positive interactive prompts block unless explicitly overridden.
findings.implication: LVX should default peer collaboration to an idle mailbox and distinct human steering.

findings.claim: Rendered-unconfirmed is honest post-write uncertainty, and delivery verification does not prove reasoning or work acceptance.
findings.implication: Separate execution, transport and quality statuses.

findings.claim: Outbox CAS and abandoned-sending recovery preserve uncertainty, but explicit claimForDelivery can reclaim indeterminate rows.
findings.implication: Do not claim universal exactly-once; retry only with effect knowledge.

findings.claim: Cancellation before write differs from interruption after input, and stop can bind expected node/session identity.
findings.implication: Separate cancel queued turn, interrupt active turn, stop process and close panel.

findings.claim: SSE handles subscription-before-replay and high-water dedup; buffer growth/live write backpressure deserves validation.
findings.confidence: Scaling concern inferred from static source; no measured performance regression.
findings.implication: Use bounded replay and snapshot sequence with explicit resync.

findings.claim: Runtime-aware context closure fails loudly; token budgets report overage without truncating pieces.
findings.implication: Retain task/output fidelity while making context cost visible.

findings.claim: React Flow graph, agent badges, activity and progressive terminals already exist, but nodes are not draggable and the terminal family is not a chat UI.
findings.implication: Borrow presentation concepts while building LVX conversation/history controls explicitly.

findings.claim: The web UI is experimental/maintenance mode; native Windows is unsupported, WSL2 is the documented route.
findings.implication: Avoid wholesale runtime/UI dependency for a native Windows studio.

findings.claim: Default permission floors and managed compaction settings differ from an untouched CLI.
findings.implication: Preserve chosen native policy; never add bypass to make orchestration succeed.

findings.claim: Inspected draft and outbox test source provides useful race fixtures but no local/live-provider verification.
findings.implication: Create LVX fixtures plus separately disclosed real native-provider smoke checks.

recommendations.action: Native adapter contract with start/runTurn/resume/interrupt/stop and optional fork, capability probing, exact effective launch metadata, provider-native conversation ID and generation.
Default to no generated project guidance, system/main-agent prompt, plugin installation, forced compaction or yolo. Pass original task unchanged; preserve omitted model/effort as provider defaults.
Durable full-text peer mailbox with IDs/body hashes, from/to and generation metadata, idle admission, one active turn per conversation and visible bounded routing.
Separate queued/admitted/started/completed/blocked execution from transport receipts and unreviewed/accepted/rejected quality; retain complete provider output and artifact paths.
Daemon-owned sessions, append-only sequenced events, bounded SSE replay, snapshot resync and cancellation that cannot later write a cancelled queued turn.
Draggable graph with provider/model/state cards, human/peer/routing edge distinctions, selected-node conversation drawer, full peer history, inspectable settings and optional native terminal.

Run untouched-CLI versus LVX acceptance trials with equal provider/model/effort, cwd snapshot and task, verifying tool behavior, context retention, full-output fidelity, resume and peer handoff before claiming model-quality parity.

Test fake CLI partial Unicode/multiline output, auth/permission gates, delayed completion, cancellation at both effect boundaries, mismatched resumes and post-write unknown outcomes; use manual native smoke checks only for installed authenticated providers.

fourPasses.implementation: Traced actual daemon, adapter, transport, state and UI source; wrote complete report and structured findings.
fourPasses.expertReread: Separated native identity, delivery render, execution completion and quality acceptance; checked model/effort and prompt mutation semantics.
fourPasses.refutation: Corrected unsupported Gemini parity, untouched-native-context assumption, universal exactly-once claim, terminal-receipt quality claim and editable/supported web canvas assumption.
fourPasses.polish: Pinned line anchors, made each recommendation concrete, recorded static-only limits and prepared artifact/source-anchor self-check. Parent depth review remains independent.

limitations: No dependency installation or external repository code executed.
Source tests inspected but not run.
No live provider sessions, credentials, private user chats or Obsidian vaults accessed.
No measured native Windows/WSL compatibility, throughput or model-quality parity.
Repository license reviewed; complete third-party dependency/license audit not performed.
